chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal narrated from Ibrahim ibn Abi Bakr ibn Abi Sammak, from Zakariyya al-Mu'min, from Isma'il ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"The one who makes up the month of Ramadan has the choice between breaking the fast (for the makeup day) and keeping it, from dawn until the sun sets; and for voluntary fasting, from dawn until the sun sets."

key_terms.زَوَالُ الشَّمْسِ: Decline of the sun (mid-afternoon, end of time for qada)
key_terms.غِيَابُ الشَّمْسِ: Sunset (end of time for voluntary fast)
key_terms.قَضَاءُ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: Making up the missed fasts of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on making up missed Ramadan fasts regarding breaking or continuing the fast?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the juristic flexibility (ikhtiyar) granted to those making up missed Ramadan fasts, allowing them to break their fast at any point before sunset or continue until sunset. This ruling extends to voluntary fasting as well, reflecting the Shia principle that the strict prohibition of breaking a fast applies primarily to the obligatory fast of Ramadan itself, while makeup and voluntary fasts offer greater leniency. The hadith is cited in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* to clarify the legal status of the 'day' in qada versus the specific timing of Maghrib.
